The normalization and commutation identities that follow justify this.

The page writes the characters chi_j, uses omega_{t_i}^{t_i}=1 to get chi_j(k+l)=chi_j(k)chi_j(l), and expands the double sum to M(F^-f)(j)(F^-g)(j). This is the paper's 'expansion of the finite sums' carried out in full.

The page gets F^+F^-=I/M by tensoring the per-axis F_t^+F_t^-=I/t. Applying F^+ gives (f*g)/M = M F^+((F^-f)(F^-g)), and dividing by r gives the displayed identity. This is correct and is the paper's route.

The page notes that L and B 'move whole records and leave each record's polynomial intact', so P(LBu,LBv)=LBP(u,v). With T_+LB=F^+ it follows that T_+ applied to the stored product equals F^+P(F^-f,F^-g), and scaling by M gives M_r(f,g).
The page defines delta=sqrt2*l*2^-p as each transform's error, citing the transform lemma's bound, and eta=sqrt2*2^-p 'for one truncation Q_p', both as in the paper.

The page uses the bilinear split P(u~,v~)-P(u,v)=P(u~-u,v~)+P(u,v~-v), bounds each term below delta using ||P(x,y)||<=||x|| ||y|| and the disk bounds on v~ and u, and so gets < 2 delta. The bound on P is itself justified ('signed sum of r products').

'truncation gives ||z~-z*||<2delta+eta': the truncation error is carried by the definition of eta. The page notes in the Cost section that Q_p keeps z~ a disk grid array, which the opposite procedure needs.

The page justifies the contraction of T_+ ('F^+ averages signed shifts and B^{-1}L^{-1} only permutes records'), uses the opposite procedure's own error below delta on z~, and applies the triangle inequality to get < 3 delta + eta, exactly as in the paper.
Scaling the exact identity M T_+ z* = M_r(f,g) by M gives error below M(3delta+eta)=sqrt2 M(3l+1)2^-p. The substitution is immediate.

The page multiplies the per-record cost O(rp log(rp)) from signed packing over the M=T/r products to get O(Tp log(rp)). It takes the three transform costs O(Tp[dK+pK^{tau-1}+l d^{lambda'}]) from the transform lemma and the scaling as linear, and sums them to the stated bound.
